mockText: 45 items in 50 minutes, with 4 drag-and-drop style items, flags and a review screen. Cisco doesn't publish the real item count or the topic weights, so this is a stand-in that fits the real 50 minutes, with an even mix across the six domains.
lead: Cisco's entry-level help desk cert. It proves you can work a ticket queue, fix common PC, Mac, phone and printer problems, get users back on the network, spot phishing and social engineering, and document what you did. A low-cost first step for anyone new to IT, and a good warm-up for A+.

cur.label: Current exam
cur.note: One exam, delivered by Pearson VUE or Certiport, in English and six other languages. No prerequisites. It's built for entry-level jobs like help desk, end user support and computer support specialist.
cur.onote: Topic list from Cisco's own 100-140 exam topic blueprint (PDF, form 4/24); titles are shortened. Cisco publishes no domain weights, so the bars show an even split.

domains.name: IT Support Job Tasks and Responsibilities
obj: Explain key help desk concepts
Queue and time management, ticketing systems, service level agreements (SLAs) and key performance indicators (KPIs).
Document customer interactions
Write a clear, factual description of the problem, the steps you tried and the result, so the next tech can pick it up.
Use a problem-solving process
Define the problem, gather details, find the likely cause, plan and make a change, watch the result, repeat if needed, and document it.

domains.name: Hardware Issues
obj: Follow basic safety practices
Electrical shock, electrostatic discharge (ESD), fire and personal safety.
Locate device information

Host name, CPU, memory, disk, OS version and IP and MAC addresses, using Task Manager, System Information, Event Viewer and ipconfig on Windows, and Activity Monitor, About This Mac and ifconfig on macOS.
Identify ports and cables
HDMI, DisplayPort, DVI, VGA, USB-A, USB-C, Micro USB, Thunderbolt, serial, RJ-45, UTP and STP, power cables and adapters.
Install and upgrade desktop components
CPU and motherboard basics, RAM, expansion cards, SATA, SSD, NVMe and M.2 storage, drivers in Device Manager, and e-waste disposal.
Troubleshoot common hardware issues
Is it plugged in and on, does the app's hardware fit (CPU, RAM, GPU, disk), Device Manager status, and the benefits and risks of firmware updates.

domains.name: Connectivity and Resource Access Issues
obj: Resolve network resource access issues
Active Directory, Entra ID and AWS IAM accounts, MFA, mapped drives (SMB and cloud), gpupdate, password resets, group membership and permissions.
Troubleshoot peripherals
Printers (queue, jams, toner), scanners, webcams, headsets, external drives, keyboards and mice, and touch displays.
Troubleshoot end-device network connectivity
Wired vs Wi-Fi, DNS and DHCP, APIPA, IPv6 link-local, subnets and gateways, SSIDs, firewalls, and ping, tracert, nslookup, netstat, ipconfig and ip.

domains.name: Operating System and Application Issues
obj: Resolve Windows issues
Display settings, BitLocker recovery keys, updates, browser cache, ending tasks, OneDrive backup and restore, Safe Mode, power and accessibility settings.
Resolve macOS issues
Display settings, app permissions, external drives, browser cache, AirDrop, Activity Monitor, iCloud and Time Machine, power and accessibility settings.
Resolve mobile device issues
Restarts, charging, connectivity, email setup, apps and basic mobile device management (MDM) on iOS and Android.
Recognize virtualization and cloud
AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, virtual machines and hypervisors, and knowing where to route a cloud incident.
Resolve common application issues
Install only approved apps, handle unknown sources, and fix email, collaboration and office apps.

domains.name: Common Threats and Preventions
obj: Identify security threats
Phishing, malware, spam, unauthorized access and spoofing; investigate, scan for malware, escalate and enforce strong passwords.
Recognize social engineering
Help desk staff are prime targets for phishing and impersonation, especially for password resets.
Protect confidential information
Spot confidential, proprietary and personally identifiable information (PII) and follow policy to protect it.

domains.name: Job Tools
obj: Use remote access software
Remote Desktop, Remote Assistance, Webex, remote management tools, TeamViewer and VNC.
Use research and documentation tools
AI tools (and their limits, ethics and privacy risks), search engines, forums and internal knowledge base articles.

extras.title: Cisco's problem-solving process
rows: Define the problem in the user's own words.
Gather details: when it started, what changed, who else is affected.
Identify the most likely cause, starting with the simple things.
Plan a change, then make it.
Not fixed? Go back to step 3 with what you learned, or escalate.
Document the cause, the fix and the result in the ticket.

extras.title: Commands that find the fault
rows: Your IP, mask, gateway and DNS. 169.254.x.x means DHCP failed.
Ping the gateway first, then an outside IP, then a name.
Shows each hop, so you see where traffic dies.
Does the name turn into the right IP address?
Which ports are open and what's connected.
gpupdate /force pulls new Group Policy, like a new mapped drive.

extras.title: Ports and cables at a glance
rows: Most monitors and TVs. DisplayPort is common on business PCs.
One port, many jobs. Thunderbolt uses the same shape.
VGA is analog. You'll still find it on projectors.
UTP for most offices; STP where there's electrical noise.
Plugs straight into the board. Much faster than SATA.

method: Use the six domains as your checklist. Hardware and connectivity cover the most ground.
Practice on your own PC: find its IP and MAC, map a share, clear a print queue, boot to Safe Mode, run the commands in the card above.
If you can, sit with your unit's help desk for a shift and watch how tickets are triaged, worked and closed.
Flashcards for ports and cables, commands, and the seven problem-solving steps.
Take timed practice sets. Fifty minutes goes fast, so practice reading a scenario and picking the FIRST step.
tips: Many answers start with the basics: is it plugged in, powered on and connected? Don't jump to reinstalling.
On any password reset or access request, confirm who you're talking to first. That's a favorite exam trap.
Know when a ticket is beyond you or your SLA. Escalating with good notes is the right answer, not a failure.
If an answer asks what to do after a fix, writing it up in the ticket is usually part of it.

items: Exam details and the link to the full topic list.
Cisco's own free courses that line up with this exam.
CCST IT Support 100-140 Official Cert Guide
The official book: every topic with review questions and practice tests.
How-tos for Safe Mode, BitLocker recovery, display and printer issues.
Activity Monitor, Time Machine, permissions and accessibility on macOS.
Free browser labs on networking and how computers talk. Good background.

quiz.q: Your queue has four new tickets. Which should you work FIRST?
o: The commanding officer's laptop can't reach the network before a briefing in 20 minutes
Right. It's urgent, high-impact and close to missing its window. Triage by impact and urgency, not by arrival time.
A user wants a second monitor installed next week
Important to the user, but not urgent. It can wait.
A ticket asking how to change a desktop background
Low impact and low urgency.
The oldest ticket in the queue, about a slow printer
First come, first served ignores impact. A slow printer is lower priority than a blocked mission task.

quiz.q: You fixed a user's VPN problem by reinstalling the client. What's the BEST ticket note?
o: VPN failed with error 809. Reinstalled the client from the software center, rebooted, user connected and confirmed. Closed.
Right. It records the symptom, the fix and the confirmation, so the next tech can repeat it.
Fixed.
Nobody can learn anything from this, and it can't help with the next ticket like it.
User broke their VPN again.
Blaming the user isn't factual and doesn't say what was done.
Tried a few things and one worked.
It doesn't say which thing worked.

quiz.q: Before you replace RAM in a desktop, what should you do FIRST?
o: Power it down, unplug it, and use an ESD strap or touch bare metal
Right. Unplugging protects you, and grounding yourself protects the parts from static.
Open the case while it's on so you can see the lights
Never work inside a powered PC.
Update the BIOS
Not required for a RAM swap, and a failed update can brick the board.
Remove the hard drive
There's no need to touch storage to change memory.

quiz.q: A user's new monitor has only USB-C and DisplayPort inputs. Their laptop has HDMI and USB-C. What's the simplest way to connect them?
o: A USB-C to USB-C cable that supports video
Right. If the laptop's USB-C port supports DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt, one cable carries video (and sometimes power).
A VGA cable
Neither device has VGA, and it's an older analog connection.
An RJ-45 patch cable
That's Ethernet. It doesn't carry video to a monitor.
A serial cable
Serial is for console and legacy devices, not displays.

quiz.q: A new design app won't install. The installer says the processor isn't supported. The PC has 32 GB of RAM and plenty of disk space. What should you check?
o: Whether the CPU architecture (for example ARM vs x64) matches what the app requires
Right. Apps are built for a processor architecture. RAM and disk can be fine while the CPU type is wrong.
The monitor's resolution
Resolution doesn't stop an app from installing.
The printer driver
Printing has nothing to do with this install error.
The user's email settings
Email isn't involved.

quiz.q: A user's laptop shows IP address 169.254.31.7 and can't reach anything. What does this tell you?
o: The laptop didn't get an address from DHCP, so it gave itself an APIPA address
Right. Check the cable or Wi-Fi connection, then whether the DHCP server or relay is reachable.
DNS is down, but everything else is fine
A DNS problem leaves you with a valid IP and only breaks names.
The laptop has a static IP set correctly
169.254.x.x is self-assigned, not a configured static address.
The user's password expired
Passwords don't change the IP address a device gets.

quiz.q: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but can't open any websites by name. Which command helps MOST next?
o: nslookup
Right. Internet access by IP works, so test whether names are turning into addresses.
tracert 8.8.8.8
The path to that IP already works.
ipconfig /release
Releasing the address would knock the user offline completely.
gpupdate /force
Group Policy doesn't fix name resolution in this case.

quiz.q: Everyone in a section lost their mapped S: drive this morning. Their accounts work. What is the MOST likely cause?
o: A change to the file share, its permissions or the group policy that maps it
Right. When a whole group loses the same resource at once, look for one shared cause, not each PC.
Every user's laptop failed overnight
Many devices failing the same way at once is very unlikely.
Their monitors are unplugged
Monitors don't affect drive mappings.
Their printer is out of toner
Unrelated to file shares.

quiz.q: After a Windows update, a laptop stops at a blue screen asking for a recovery key. What is the user seeing?
o: The BitLocker recovery screen; look up the key in the approved directory after verifying the user
Right. BitLocker asks for its recovery key after some firmware or boot changes. Confirm identity, then get the key through the approved process.
A virus demanding ransom
A ransom note asks for payment. This is Windows' own recovery prompt.
A failed hard drive
A dead drive gives disk errors, not a BitLocker key prompt.
A screen saver password
The screen saver lock appears after login, not at boot.

quiz.q: A program has frozen on a Mac and won't close. What's the right tool?
o: Force Quit, or Activity Monitor to end the process
Right. That's the macOS equivalent of ending a task in Task Manager.
Time Machine
Time Machine restores backups. It doesn't stop a running app.
AirDrop
AirDrop shares files between Apple devices.
Disk Utility's erase option
Erasing a drive destroys data. It's not how you close an app.

quiz.q: A user asks you to install a free screen-capture tool they found on a website. It's not on the approved software list. What should you do?
o: Decline, explain the policy, and offer an approved tool or the request process
Right. Unknown sources can carry malware. Stick to approved software and the process to add new tools.
Install it, since it's free
Free doesn't mean safe or approved.
Give the user admin rights so they can install it
That violates least privilege and spreads the risk.
Download it on your own PC first to test it
That just puts the risk on your machine instead.

quiz.q: A caller says they're the new chief, locked out and in a hurry, and asks you to reset their password and read the new one over the phone. What should you do?
o: Verify their identity with the approved method before any reset
Right. Urgency and authority are classic social engineering pressure. Verify first, every time.
Reset it right away because they outrank you
Rank isn't verification. Attackers count on this.
Ask for their old password to confirm who they are
The help desk should never ask for passwords.
Email the new password to whatever address they give you
An address the caller supplies could be the attacker's.

quiz.q: A user forwards an email from 'IT Support' asking everyone to log in at a link to keep their mailbox. The link goes to a look-alike domain. What should you do FIRST?
o: Tell the user not to click, and report it through the phishing or security process
Right. It's phishing. Report it so security can block it and warn others.
Click the link to see what it does
Never test a phishing link on a work system.
Reply to the sender and ask if it's real
That talks to the attacker and confirms an active mailbox.
Ignore it, since only one user saw it
Phishing usually goes to many people. Reporting protects everyone.

quiz.q: You want to use a public AI chatbot to help write a troubleshooting article. What should you avoid putting in it?
o: User names, PII, hostnames, passwords and internal system details
Right. Public AI tools may keep what you paste. Keep sensitive and internal data out, and check the AI's answer before you use it.
A general description of the error message
Generic, non-sensitive text is the safe way to use these tools, where policy allows.
The name of the operating system
That's general information.
A request to fix your grammar
Harmless.

pbqs.title: Work the help desk queue
pbqs.scenario: Six tickets are waiting. Read each one and pick the most likely fix. Each answer is used once; two options are distractors.

items.log:
> ipconfig
Ethernet adapter: Media disconnected
Wi-Fi: not connected
items.why: The adapter reports no link at all. Check the cable, the port, or connect to Wi-Fi first.

items.log:
> ping 8.8.8.8
Reply from 8.8.8.8: time=21ms
> nslookup intranet
*** Can't find server name for address 10.0.0.9: Timed out
items.why: Traffic by IP works; the DNS server it's pointed at doesn't answer. Fix the DNS setting or the server.

items.log:
Queue: 14 documents
First job: 'Error - Printing' (stuck since 08:02)
Printer: online, paper OK, toner 60%
items.why: One stuck job is blocking the rest. Clear or restart the queue.

items.log:
BitLocker recovery
Enter the recovery key for this drive
Recovery key ID: 4F2A...
items.why: BitLocker wants its key. Verify the user, then get the key from the approved directory.

items.log:
Caller: locked out after vacation, password expired.
Account status: locked (password expired)
items.why: A routine lockout. Verify the caller's identity, then reset.

items.log:
Power on: 3 long beeps, no display
Ticket note: user's coworker added a memory stick yesterday
items.why: Beep codes right after a memory change point to RAM that isn't seated. Power off and reseat it.

pbqs.title: Prioritize and route
pbqs.scenario: For each ticket, pick its priority and where it goes. Some options aren't used.

rows.req: User clicked a phishing link and entered their password
rows.why: A possible compromise is urgent. Report to security right away so they can reset and investigate.
Many users down at once is high priority, and the cause is likely in the network, not each PC.
Low impact and easy to fix yourself: swap the mouse.

rows.req: Shared mailbox needs a new member added
rows.why: Normal access change you can handle with approval.

rows.req: The cloud-hosted training site is down for everyone
rows.why: It's hosted in the cloud, so route it to the provider (through your team's process) after confirming it isn't local.

keep.text: A CCST earned on or after July 15, 2025 is valid for 5 years. One earned before that date doesn't expire.
keep.after: Renew by passing any current CCST, associate, professional or expert Cisco exam. Continuing education credits don't count for CCST.

keep.text: CCST IT Support isn't on the DoD 8140 qualification matrix. On its own it won't qualify you for a coded billet.
keep.after: For the Technical Support Specialist (411) role, A+, Network+ and Security+ are Basic options.

keep.text: At $125 it's a cheap, quick proof that you can work a help desk, and good practice before A+.
keep.after: Add the Credly badge to your résumé and LinkedIn.
